Dzyhivka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Dzyhivka's Jewish community grew after King Stanisław August Poniatowski — the last king of Poland — officially proclaimed the town a market center in 1787, drawing in a large Jewish population; by the early 1900s the town supported five synagogues. Between 1923 and 1926, Dzyhivka natives founded three Soviet Jewish agricultural colonies in the Kherson region — part of the same wave of Jewish farm-colony settlement documented at several other sites in this collection. Under Romanian administration from 1941, a labor ghetto held local Jews alongside deportees from Bessarabia and Bukovina; only 105 remained alive by September 1943. By 1998, just 12 elderly Jewish residents remained in Dzyhivka; none live there today.
